messages:
Alicia F.: heads up — saw a GCP notice this morning: egress surcharge + change to sustained use discounts for europe-west1. this could push our eu unit cost up significantly. can finance + infra triage impact on committed/reserved plans?

Raj P.: link? do we have the announcement text?

Alicia F.: https://cloud.google.com/announcements/example (summary: 12% egress surcharge on certain classes, sustained-use discount reduced from 30% -> 20% over long-running GPUs) :frowning:

billing-bot: GCP billing alert generated for project:redwood-prod — potential monthly delta estimate: +$92k based on current usage patterns. See dashboard: https://billing.internal/reports/2030-eu-gcp-delta

Victor S.: cluster health wise we saw higher egress already last week during model syncs, but most cross-region traffic was small. main risk is scheduled downloads and model sync spikes.

Mei L.: two quick notes: 1) shifting inference to us-central would avoid the egress surcharge but adds ~35ms median latency for EU customers. 2) we could staged-shift non-latency-sensitive batch workloads to another region. both need capacity adjustments + commit alignment.

Clara M.: product question — if we need to pass through some costs to enterprise, need to know magnitude. small customers we probably absorb. :thinking_face:

Alicia F.: agreed. we need a quick unit-econ check (delta on gross margin per token and per-dedicated-gpu) and then options for commitments: a) renegotiate reserved price in eu with cloud sales b) shift reserved pool to a different region c) absorb and adjust packaging.

Raj P.: I'll run the allocation model and a worst-case scenario on reserved capacity. returning numbers in ~2 hours. can someone pull the per-region token/hour numbers?

Victor S.: pasted quick query results from metrics (last 30d):
```
region,effective_gpu_hours,egress_gb
europe-west1,14,3200
us-central1,10,800
asia-east1,4,200
```

Mei L.: also note regulatory constraints for some enterprise customers (FR/DE) — can't move to us-central. that'll limit mitigation for ~18% of EU committed capacity.

Raj P.: quick back-of-envelope using Victor numbers:
```
old_gpu_hour_cost_eu = $1.25
new_gpu_hour_cost_eu = $1.40  # after discount change + surcharge
delta_hour = 0.15
monthly_delta = delta_hour * europe_hours_per_month (~14*24*30*#gpus) -> depends on committed pool
```
I'll plug committed pool sizes into the model and post spreadsheet.

Alicia F.: target asks: 1) delta $/token and $/hour for current committed pools, 2) delta if we moved 30% of batch load to us-central, 3) negotiation ask for cloud sales (target $X/hr or credit) and fallback pricing changes to customers if needed.

Clara M.: I can draft two customer comms: one for enterprise (negotiation heads-up) and a short FAQ if we need to adjust packaging. leave placeholders until we have numbers.

Raj P.: uploaded preliminary sheet: https://docs.internal/sheets/2030012345-eu-commit-impact - early numbers show ~9-12% gross margin compression on hosted tokens if we do nothing.

Mei L.: engineering constraints: shifting 30% batch -> us-central would require cross-region routing rules + KV cache warming; estimate 2-week effort to automate safely. manual first step: routing based on customer tags.

Victor S.: on infra ops: we can reduce egress by enabling model delta sync (rsync with diffs) for scheduled syncs — could cut model sync egress by ~60% for large models. low effort change.

Alicia F.: ok action list: - Raj run full committed-pool sensitivity and post final numbers by EOD. - Mei prototype routing rules and check cache impact (P0 for batch). - Victor implement delta-sync for model syncs and estimate savings. - Clara draft comms templates. finance will prepare pricing scenarios.

Raj P.: will do. quick note: committed contracts renew in 45/90/180 day buckets across EU fleets — prioritizing the 45-day renewals gives most leverage.

Clara M.: adding to roadmap: update enterprise pricing doc + run legal on potential T&C updates for pass-through charges.

Alicia F.: thanks all. please drop final numbers in this thread so we have a single source. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: scheduled report seeded: eu-gcp-delta-2030012345.csv saved to /billing/deltas/2030/ — expected variance column included.
